questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

The situation was __out of hand__. So, the manager called the police station for help.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. To be uncontrollable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"uncontrollable"** means something that cannot be controlled or restrained. (अनियंत्रित)

 
 
• **Example:** The wildfire became uncontrollable, spreading rapidly across the forest.
 
 
 
• **"Out of hand"** refers to a situation that has become uncontrollable or chaotic. (नियंत्रण से बाहर)
 
 
• **Example:** The protest got out of hand, leading to clashes with the police.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the meaning of **'out of hand'** is **'to be uncontrollable'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. To be uncontrollable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To be serious** (गंभीर होना): Being earnest or solemn in nature.

 
 
• **Example:** The teacher asked the students to be serious during the examination.
 
 
 
• **In an undecided state** (अनिर्णीत अवस्था में): Being in a state where a decision has not been made.
 
 
• **Example:** The match was left in an undecided state due to the rain.
 
 
 
• **To be abrupt** (अचानक होना): Being sudden or unexpected.
 
 
• **Example:** His decision to resign was quite abrupt and surprised everyone.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

My mother asked me who __did accompany__ me to the airport.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. who accompanied me .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the past tense, as indicated by the verb "asked".
 
• The correct form of the verb to use in the past tense is "accompanied".
 
• The correct substitution for "who did accompany me" is "who accompanied me".

Correct sentence: *My mother asked me who **accompanied** me to the airport*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Past Simple Tense:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + past form of the verb.
 
• **Example:** She visited the museum.
 
• **Usage:** Describes actions completed in the past.
 
 
 
• **Past Continuous Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure: **Subject + was/were + base verb + -ing.
 
• **Example: **They were watching a movie.
 
• **Usage: **Describes actions that were ongoing in the past.

questions.question:

Correct sentence: *He was acquitted of a cyber crime on the basis of evidence given to the court*.

questions.question: Select the option that has an error in the use of phrasal verb.

options.text: Back up your essential files. Technology is only sometimes reliable.
Pushpa came across an old photo in the album and asked me to recognise the face in it.
Please turn up the heater. The weather is too cold today.
Please suggest me some tips to get out nervousness.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. Please suggest me some tips to get out nervousness .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence contains an error in the use of the phrasal verb.
 
• In the context of providing suggestions or advice, the correct phrasing is "Please suggest some tips" without the use of "me."
 
• The phrase "to get out nervousness" is also incorrect. The correct phrase should be "to overcome nervousness" or "to get rid of nervousness."

Correct sentence: *Please suggest some tips to overcome nervousness*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common Phrasal Verbs:**
 
 
• **Back up:** To make a copy of data (e.g., Back up your essential files).
 
• **Came across:** To find something by chance (e.g., Pushpa came across an old photo).
 
• **Turn up:** To increase the volume or intensity (e.g., Please turn up the heater).
 
 
 
• **Correct Usage:**
 
 
• **Suggest:** Should be used without "me" when giving general advice (e.g., Please suggest some tips).
 
• **Overcome/Get rid of:** Appropriate phrases to express dealing with nervousness (e.g., to overcome nervousness).
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Leif Erikson is a Viking _______ believed to have sailed from the Green Lands to Vinland. Vinland is now thought to be at the northern tip of Canada’s Newfoundland island where _______ found evidence of Erikson’s _______ in 1960s.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. explorer; archaeologists; settlement .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage talks about Leif Erikson, who is historically known as a Viking explorer.
 
• Vinland is associated with Norse exploration, so the term "archaeologists" is appropriate for those who found evidence.
 
• "Settlement" is the most fitting term to describe the area where Erikson's group lived.

Correct sentence: *Leif Erikson is a Viking **explorer** believed to have sailed from the Green Lands to Vinland. Vinland is now thought to be at the northern tip of Canada's Newfoundland island where **archaeologists** found evidence of Erikson's **settlement** in 1960s.*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1st Conditional Sentence:**

 
 
• **Structure:** If + Present Simple, will + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If it rains, we will cancel the picnic.
 
• **Usage: **Describes real or possible situations in the future with likely outcomes.
 
 
 
• **2nd Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure:** If + past simple, would + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If I were an astronaut, I would look at the stars all the time.
 
• **Usage: **Used to talk about hypothetical situations.
 
 
 
• **3rd Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure: **If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle.
 
• **Example: **If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
 
• **Usage: **Refers to unreal past situations and their imagined outcomes.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase.

This __sentence can have multiple meanings__. Could you please specify what it means?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Ambiguous .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence can have multiple meanings, which makes it **ambiguous**.
 
• An **ambiguous** statement is one that is open to more than one interpretation.
 
• This implies that the meaning is not clear and can be understood in different ways by different people.

Correct sentence: *This sentence can have multiple meanings. Could you please specify what it means?*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Homogeneous:**

 
 
• Definition: Composed of parts or elements that are all of the same kind.
 
• Example: The population of the small town was fairly homogeneous.
 
• Usage: Used to describe things that are uniform or similar in nature.
 
 
 
• **Amorphous:**
 
 
• Definition: Lacking a clear structure or focus.
 
• Example: The project had an amorphous plan that led to confusion.
 
• Usage: Used to describe things that are shapeless or lack a defined form.
 
 
 
• **Heterogeneous:**
 
 
• Definition: Composed of different kinds or types.
 
• Example: The committee was made up of a heterogeneous group of individuals.
 
• Usage: Used to describe things that are diverse or varied.

• **Example:** The movie was horrifying and scared everyone.
 
• **Usage: **Used to describe something that causes a feeling of horror.
 
 
 
• **Horrified:**
 
 
• **Meaning: **Feeling or showing horror or shock.
 
• **Example: **She was horrified by the news.
 
• **Usage: **Used to describe someone's reaction to something shocking or horrifying.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The gold watch / look really expensive / and is not affordable / for common people.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. look really expensive .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence should use the verb form that agrees with the subject "The gold watch."
 
• The correct form is "looks" instead of "look" because "The gold watch" is a singular subject.
 
• The structure of the sentence should be corrected to "The gold watch looks really expensive and is not affordable for common people."

Correct sentence: *The gold watch **looks** really expensive and is not affordable for common people.*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:**
 
 
• **Rule:** A singular subject requires a singular verb, and a plural subject requires a plural verb.
 
• **Example:** She **runs** every day. (singular subject and verb)
 
• **Example:** They **run** every day. (plural subject and verb)
 
 
 
• **Verb Tense Consistency:**
 
 
• Ensure that the verbs in a sentence are consistent in their tense.
 
• **Example:** He **was** walking and **talking** at the same time. (both verbs in past continuous)
 
 
</ul

questions.question:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Restraint"** means a measure or condition that keeps someone or something under control; the action of keeping someone or something under control. (संयम)

 
 
• **Example: **He showed great restraint in dealing with the difficult situation.
 
 
 
• **"Self-control"** refers to the ability to control oneself, in particular one's emotions and desires, especially in difficult situations. (आत्म-संयम)
 
 
• **Example: **Practicing self-control can help you manage stress and avoid impulsive decisions.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is: **Self-control**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Self-esteem** (आत्म-सम्मान): Confidence in one's own worth or abilities.

 
 
• **Example:** Building self-esteem is crucial for personal development.
 
 
 
• **Self-acceptance** (आत्म-स्वीकृति): Acceptance of oneself, including one's own strengths and weaknesses.

• The phrase **"across all his faults"** is incorrect. The correct phrase should be **"despite all his faults"** or **"in spite of all his faults"**.

• Correcting this phrase will make the sentence grammatically correct and meaningful.

Correct sentence: *It has been noticed that despite all his faults, he is admired.*.

• **Despite:** Used before a noun or pronoun. Example: Despite the rain, we went for a walk.
 
• **In spite of:** Used before a noun or pronoun. Example: In spite of his injury, he completed the race.
 
 
 
• **Other similar phrases:**
 
 
• **Even though:** Used before a clause. Example: Even though he was tired, he continued working.
 
• **Although:** Used before a clause. Example: Although it was late, they stayed up talking.
